title: 7 October 2017 SMRT Flooding Incident and Related Issues
what_it_is: 7 October 2017 SMRT Flooding Incident and Related Issues

sections.label: Flooding reported between Bishan and Braddell
sections.summary: A train captain reported flooding on southbound tracks between Bishan and Braddell, and SMRT suspended services between Ang Mo Kio and Toa Payoh.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: [Please refer to "Measures to Prevent Future Flooding in MRT Tunnel", Official Report, 6 November 2017, Vol 94, Issue No 53, Written Answers to Questions for Oral Answer not Answered by End of Question Time section.] Mr Speaker, on 7 October at 5.14 pm, an alert SMRT train captain, Mr Choo Ah Heng, reported flooding on the southbound tunnel tracks between Bishan and Braddell MRT stations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: At 5.30 pm, the SMRT Operations Control Centre (OCC) suspended train services on both bounds between Ang Mo Kio and Toa Payoh MRT stations.

sections.label: Flood waters cleared overnight
sections.summary: After the arcing incident was resolved, multiple agencies worked through the night to clear flood waters up to one metre deep covering 100 metres of tracks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Although the electrical arcing incident was resolved and services resumed between Marina South Pier and Newton by 9.22 pm, it took multiple agencies working through the night to clear the flood waters between Bishan and Braddell MRT stations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: These flood waters were up to one metre deep and covered 100 metres of tracks on both bounds.

sections.label: Full resumption and disruption duration
sections.summary: Train services fully resumed at 1.36 pm after safety and operational tests, with a cumulative disruption of 14.5 hours over Saturday and Sunday.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Train services fully resumed at 1.36 pm, after various safety and operational tests and checks to the tracks were completed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: This flood incident resulted in a cumulative disruption to service of 14.5 hours: seven hours on Saturday and 7.5 hours on Sunday.

sections.label: Poor maintenance by SMRT team
sections.summary: The system could manage even an extraordinary storm if well-maintained, but the flood was due to poor maintenance and neglect by the SMRT team responsible for the Bishan sump pump system.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Even if it were an extraordinary storm, like what Penang experienced a couple of days ago, the system, if well-maintained, would be able to manage it.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: It was due to poor maintenance and neglect of duties by the specific SMRT maintenance team responsible for the Bishan storm water sump pump system.

sections.label: Rainfall cleared from tunnels
sections.summary: The total rainfall cleared from the tunnels was about 640 cubic metres, much less than the 5,000-cubic-metre capacity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: In comparison, the total rainfall which was cleared from the tunnels was only about 640 cubic metres, not even 700, not even 1,000 cubic metres, much less than the 5,000-cubic-metre capacity.

sections.label: Bishan sump pumps functional
sections.summary: While LTA investigations are ongoing, all three pumps in the Bishan storm water sump pit were functional as they could be manually activated after flooding was discovered.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: While investigations by LTA are still on-going, we know now that all three pumps in the Bishan storm water sump pit were functional, as they could be manually activated after the flooding was discovered.

sections.label: Bishan anti-flooding system maintenance
sections.summary: Findings indicate the Bishan anti-flooding system had not been maintained for several months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Based on their findings, it appears that the Bishan anti-flooding system had not been maintained for several months.

sections.label: Maintenance records possibly falsified
sections.summary: The maintenance records may have been falsified.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: In other words, the maintenance records may have been falsified.

sections.label: Pumps not in serviceable condition
sections.summary: SMRT found two of eight pumps at Kembangan and three of four at Lavender were not serviceable.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: SMRT found that two out of eight pumps at Kembangan and three out of four pumps at Lavender were not in serviceable condition.

sections.label: SMRT suspends managerial staff
sections.summary: SMRT suspended him and six other managerial staff over their discharge of supervisory responsibilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: SMRT has suspended him, together with six other managerial staff, with respect to their discharge of supervisory responsibilities.

sections.label: No Committee of Inquiry
sections.summary: The Ministry will therefore not convene a Committee of Inquiry.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: My Ministry will, therefore, not be convening a Committee of Inquiry.

sections.label: Sludge, silt and debris removal
sections.summary: Removal of accumulated sludge, silt and debris in the sump pit is in progress.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: The removal of accumulated sludge, silt and debris in the sump pit is also in progress.

sections.label: SMRT replaces Vice President
sections.summary: SMRT replaced Vice President Mr Ng Tek Poo with senior mechanical engineer Mr Siu Yow Wee.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: SMRT has replaced the Vice President, Mr Ng Tek Poo, with Mr Siu Yow Wee, a senior mechanical engineer with SMRT.

sections.label: Anti-flooding maintenance frequency increased
sections.summary: Anti-flooding maintenance frequency was increased from quarterly to monthly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Second, it has increased the frequency of anti-flooding maintenance from quarterly to monthly.

sections.label: Taipei Metro experts review SMRT
sections.summary: SMRT invited Taipei Metro experts to independently review its operations and recommend improvements in system management, engineering and maintenance.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Fourth, it has invited a team of experts from the Taipei Metro to do a thorough and independent review of its operations, to flush out any gaps and recommend improvements in the areas of system management, engineering and maintenance.

sections.label: SMRT Chairman on audits
sections.summary: SMRT Chairman Seah Moon Ming stated zero tolerance for supervision failures and said the Board will review senior management remuneration.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: SMRT's new Chairman, Mr Seah Moon Ming − he is here in the Public Gallery − has publicly stated that his company has zero tolerance for failures in supervision and diligence over maintenance tasks and will be undertaking a comprehensive audit of maintenance records and practices to uncover any lapses or impropriety.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: He has also shared that the Board will review the remuneration of its senior management, from the CEO through the relevant chain of command.

sections.label: CEO comments on cultural issues
sections.summary: At a media conference on 16 October 2017, SMRT CEO Desmond Kuek commented on deep-seated cultural issues within SMRT.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: At a media conference on 16 October 2017, CEO of SMRT Desmond Kuek commented on some "deep-seated cultural issues" within SMRT.

sections.label: LTA and SMRT pump review
sections.summary: LTA stressed tunnel sump pump maintenance, SMRT agreed to list pumps for replacement, and a Joint Readiness Inspection team will be set up.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Nonetheless, during a recent meeting with SMRT on 29 September 2017, just a few days before the tunnel flooding incident, LTA had stressed the importance of maintaining tunnel sump pump systems.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: SMRT, subsequently, agreed to review and surface a list of pumps requiring replacement to LTA.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, the incident occurred before this review could be completed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: There has been no shortcoming or lapses in oversight by LTA staff in the present regulatory framework.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Going forward, I have asked LTA to partner SMRT and to set up a new Joint Readiness Inspection team to supplement SMRT's own internal audit system.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: At SMRT Chairman Seah Moon Ming's request, ST Kinetics has released Dr Richard Kwok to head SMRT's augmented audit team.

sections.label: LTA and rail operators relationship
sections.summary: The fourth unspoken role is to cultivate a trust-based relationship between LTA and rail operators towards reliable rail transport.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: That is the sort of work relationship which I am familiar with, which I think is the only way to achieve any kind of excellence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: So, this fourth and unspoken role is to cultivate this relationship between LTA and the rail operators founded on trust and constructive collaboration towards a common mission of providing a reliable rail transport.

sections.label: Mean Kilometres Between Failure metric
sections.summary: The international train reliability metric is Mean Kilometres Between Failure of more than five minutes, and MRT improved from 133,000 in 2015 to 425,000 train-kilometres this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: The metric for measuring train reliability internationally is the Mean Kilometres Between Failure (MKBF) of more than five minutes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: For our MRT network, it has improved significantly from 133,000 train-kilometres in 2015, that is two years ago, to now 425,000 train-kilometres this year.

sections.label: Improvement across five MRT lines
sections.summary: The improvement is real and significant and is experienced by all five MRT lines, including the oldest North-South and East-West Lines.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: The improvement is real and significant and is experienced by all the five MRT lines, including the oldest North-South and East-West Lines.

sections.label: Re-signalling North-South and East-West Lines
sections.summary: Re-signalling of the North-South Line and, next year, the East-West Line is a very major project with its own attendant problems.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Re-signalling of North-South and, next year, East-West Line is a very major project with its own attendant problems, which I have discussed in this House many months ago.

sections.label: Commuters lose faith in MKBF
sections.summary: Signalling system change problems mean commuters cannot relate to improved MKBF, and disruptions including the 7 October flooding have made commuters lose faith.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Back to the North-South Line, because we do have problems with the change of the signalling system, commuters cannot relate with this so-called, from their point of view, improved MKBF and their actual real life experience.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: And other disruptions, both in the past and now, the flooding on 7 October, have made commuters lose faith.

sections.label: Asset renewal on oldest lines
sections.summary: To sustain progress, asset renewal works on the oldest lines must be completed as soon as possible.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: To sustain the progress we are making, asset renewal works on our oldest lines must be completed as soon as possible.

sections.label: MKBF one million target 2020
sections.summary: The aim to cross an MKBF of one million train-kilometres by 2020 is within reach.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Our aim to cross an MKBF of one million train-kilometres by 2020 is within our grasp.

sections.label: Renewing North-South East-West Lines
sections.summary: Plans renew six core components of the North-South and East-West Lines, about halfway through a journey ending in 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: In September this year, I shared with this House our urgent plans to renew the six core components of the North-South and East-West Lines.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: These are the sleepers, third rail, signalling system, power supply, track circuits and the old train, the first-generation trains.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: We are about halfway through this multi-year journey, with our final destination in 2024.

sections.label: Ageing lines risk major disruptions
sections.summary: Until key ageing systems are replaced or renewed, the North-South and East-West Lines remain at risk of major disruptions despite diligent maintenance.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Until all these key ageing systems are replaced or renewed, the North-South and East-West Lines remain at risk of major disruptions, even with diligent maintenance.

sections.label: Raising train reliability and rail workers
sections.summary: The speaker cites aligned appointments and agency expertise, keeps the 2020 MKBF target, and describes rail maintenance workers' tight time constraints.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: I asked around and I persuaded PSD to post him to me when Mr Chew Men Leong, his predecessor, decided to leave for personal reason.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: So, I think the planets are now very well-aligned − you have me in MOT, Ngien Hoon Ping in LTA, Permanent Secretary Loh Ngai Seng in MOT and Chairman Seah Moon Ming in SMRT.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Other agencies, especially PUB, DSTA, DSO and GovTech, have offered their expertise to help us in this journey.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: This gives me the confidence that we can complete this job of raising train reliability.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: I have not changed my target of achieving an MKBF of one million train-kilometres by 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: We just have to lean in, re-double our efforts and work smarter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I now speak as the Executive Secretary of the National Transport Workers' Union.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The demands on our rail workers are much greater than before, particularly for the maintenance staff.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Many of our rail maintenance workers work hard to ensure that our rail systems are maintained properly, are functioning properly every day, 365 days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: They work in a challenging environment and under very tight time constraints − about three hours every night is the amount of time that they have.

sections.label: LTA fit and proper criteria questions
sections.summary: Two questions ask whether LTA will impose a fit and proper criteria regime and whether it identified any rail asset maintenance backlog.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: First, does LTA intend to impose a fit and proper criteria regime on the senior management of rapid transit system operators?

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Second, has LTA identified any backlog in maintenance of its rail assets to date and, if so, what action has been taken?

sections.label: Change of financing system
sections.summary: One major thing accomplished was the change of the financing system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: One major thing that we have accomplished was the change of the financing system.

sections.label: SMRT cultural issues make-up
sections.summary: The Member asks the Minister to shed light on the rough make-up of the 10% on deep-seated cultural issues within SMRT.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: My clarifications are: on these deep-seated cultural issues within SMRT, can the Minister shed some light on the rough make-up of the 10%?

sections.label: Monthly maintenance and track access
sections.summary: The press conference mentioned the crew has problems getting track access because of other maintenance when frequency increased from quarterly to monthly.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: On increasing the frequency of maintenance from quarterly to monthly, it was mentioned in the press conference that the crew has problems getting access to the tracks because of other maintenance.

sections.label: Sump pump failure cause
sections.summary: The sump pump failure was caused by no maintenance, not by lack of frequency.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: The cause of the sump pump failure is because of no maintenance and not because of lack of frequency.

sections.label: Falsified records and SMRT fines
sections.summary: The Member asks whether the Ministry would review its earlier recommendation of not fining SMRT after falsified maintenance records, and how this impacts the Thomson-East Coast Line contract framework.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: After the new revelation last week on the falsified maintenance records, would the Ministry review its earlier recommendation of not fining SMRT?

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: How would this also impact the incentive and disincentive framework that is part of the Thomson-East Coast Line contract?

sections.label: Faulty pumps at four stations
sections.summary: The Member says access was quoted as an issue for water pump maintenance, but the team did not ask for access, so it was an untrue excuse.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: My last clarification is on the faulty pumps found in the other four stations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: As I have explained in my Statement, access was quoted as an issue for the water pump maintenance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: But as the Member has heard, the team did not even bother to ask for access.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: So, it was an excuse which turned out to be not true at all.

sections.label: Re-introducing incentive and penalty system
sections.summary: The Member says for North-South and East-West Lines, the incentive/penalty system could be re-introduced after stabilising, perhaps defined as reaching one million MKBF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: To me, for North-South Line, East-West Line, I think we are in transition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: And until you stabilise, "stabilise" perhaps defined as when you reach one million MKBF, then, maybe, at that time, you can re-introduce this incentive/penalty system to encourage above-average performance, as well as to discourage sub-average outcome.

sections.label: Bishan storm pit size
sections.summary: The Bishan storm pit is unusually huge at 5,000 cubic metres, while all the others are tiny.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: Bishan storm pit is very unusual by its size.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: It is huge − 5,000 cubic metres − whereas all the others are tiny.

sections.label: SMRT suspends supervisors
sections.summary: SMRT suspended supervisors and former supervisors, saying managers responsible for checking the team were negligent too.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: In yesterday's press statement, SMRT went further to suspend their supervisors and former supervisors because this is a failure not just of the small team but, clearly, the managers who were responsible to check and double-check the team were negligent as well.

sections.label: SMRT maintenance regime transformation
sections.summary: One call was for profound transformation of SMRT's maintenance regime, with LTA imposing a maintenance management system audit and SMRT self-assessing every three to four years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: One of which was calling for a profound transformation of the maintenance regime at SMRT.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: There was a requirement for LTA to impose and implement a maintenance management system audit on SMRT and for SMRT to perform a self-assessment every three to four years.

sections.label: Oversight of SMRT audits
sections.summary: The Member asked whether an independent entity will oversee SMRT's coming audits, their nature, and if findings will be public; the Minister spoke of embedding LTA audit compliance inspectors in SMRT.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In light of this, can I ask the Minister, with regard to the audits that are going to be carried out by SMRT in the weeks and the months to come, will there be an independent entity overseeing these audits, what will be their nature and will their findings be made public?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Minister spoke of embedding LTA staff in SMRT, specifically audit compliance inspectors, to assist in maintenance.

sections.label: LTA engineers embedded in SMRT
sections.summary: More engineers were brought on board, with a significant number of LTA engineers embedded in SMRT and on the ground.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: One, beef up, get more engineers on board and with the view to also embed quite a number of them in SMRT and it was done.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: So, quite a significant number of LTA engineers are actually on the ground with SMRT.

sections.label: MKBF improvement explained
sections.summary: The Minister lacked details to reply immediately but said those implementations were done, explaining the MKBF improvement, especially in the last two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: I do not have the details and the information to reply to the Member immediately but those implementations were done.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: And that explains the improvement in the MKBF, especially in the last two years.

sections.label: Instilling pride in SMRT staff
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Ministry or SMRT is looking into instilling pride in staff jobs, saying audits cannot surface all lapses.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am sure the Minister's vision or ambition of having one million MKBF would be achievable soon.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I know Mr Seah Moon Ming and Mr Richard Kwok personally as we have worked in the Institute of Engineers.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Based on what has been reported so far, I think what is lacking in some of the staff is the pride in their jobs.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I think no amount of audit can surface all the lapses or shortcomings.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: How can this pride in their jobs be instilled?

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Is the Ministry or SMRT looking into this aspect?

sections.label: SMRT amnesty and union discussion
sections.summary: The speaker says SMRT must answer on amnesty, that owning up is treated generously, and advises SMRT to discuss it with the union.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: On the first question on the amnesty and how it will be handled, that has to be answered by SMRT.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: If you come forward, you own up on doing something that you should not do or forgot to do or did not do well a few weeks ago, then management will take that into account and, generally, the approach is to be generous.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: How amnesty works is if, for example, you did something stupid and you never owned up and when the inspection team discovers that, then you will get into serious trouble.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: But as I have said, it is something new for SMRT.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: I will advise them to discuss with the union to find out how best to do it with a view to quickly uncover gaps and, secondly, use the opportunity to forge a closer relationship between employer and the employees. on track design and are there better ways so that it is more resilient: a couple of years ago, I was quite puzzled how New York Underground was able to run 24 hours.

sections.label: Two parties' market share
sections.summary: Together, they account for 60-odd percent of the total market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: Together, they account for 60-odd percent of the total market.

sections.label: Fines and SMRT management remuneration
sections.summary: The speaker cites the $5.4 million fine on SMRT and proposes pegging management remuneration to reliability and rewarding workers financially.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The highest fine imposed to-date was $5.4 million on SMRT for the 7 July 2015 breakdown disrupting 413,000 commuters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Yet, that money was less than 0.5% of SMRT's total revenue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Second, we should peg the remuneration of SMRT's management to the overall reliability of SMRT and, where milestones are met by workers slogging it out, working their guts out in the tunnels, reward them with financial recognition.

sections.label: Seah Moon Ming as new Chairman
sections.summary: The speaker says he gave names including Mr Seah Moon Ming, who is now the new Chairman, and regrets the delay.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: Over the months, I gave him names, including Mr Seah Moon Ming, and that is how Mr Seah Moon Ming is now the new Chairman.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: My only disappointment is it took so long before we got this done.

sections.label: Joint LTA and cross-audit team
sections.summary: The speaker says LTA will work with Dr Richard Kwok on a joint team and operators' staff will cross-audit each other.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: The experts and the extent of audits, in particular, the inspection team that we are setting up, it will be as extensive as needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: But LTA will be coming in to work together with Dr Richard Kwok to form a joint team.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: What we have in mind is also to cross-audit the other operators and make use of some of their staff to cross-audit each other so that Operator One can also join in the auditing of Operator Two.

sections.label: London Underground re-signalling testing lesson
sections.summary: The London Underground re-signalling project taught the speaker to do more testing without passengers and debug as much as possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: The main takeaway for us from the London Underground re-signalling project was, do many more testing without passengers and debug as much as you can.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: Testing was supposed to start in January this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: That, I think, has saved us a lot of trouble and we were able to stabilise the system within a few months rather than the whole year that London Underground took.

sections.label: Outsourcing SMRT non-core waterpump work
sections.summary: The Member asks whether LTA can work with SMRT to outsource non-core work like waterpumps so management can focus on core business.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: The Minister has used the phrase "小儿科" in discovering the maintenance of those pumps and has also described it as low-risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: I completely agree with the Minister because these are waterpumps, these are not cardiovascular pumps that you put in your heart, which is quite different.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: So, with that in mind, I would like to ask the Minister whether it is possible for LTA to work with SMRT to outsource some of these what I would describe as non-core business that we are doing, so that the management of SMRT today can focus on its core competency, its core businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: Of course, it is good if you have the management bandwidth to also cover these without having to outsource, but when we are so short of time and have so many things to deal with, the quickest way, actually, is to outsource non-core.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: In that case, selection of contractors becomes very important.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: And, again, here we can learn from others − water, anti-flooding type of things, PUB will know which are the good contractors in town.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: I am told that the SMRT Chairman is seriously thinking about working on this strategy.

sections.label: Disagreement on SMRT profit purpose
sections.summary: The speaker disagrees with the Member's preamble that SMRT is there to make money for the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: Before I reply to the Member's two clarifications, I think I must disagree with the Member's preamble that SMRT is there to make money for the Government.

sections.label: Not losing money objective
sections.summary: The speaker states that making money is not the objective but losing money must be avoided.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: Making money is not your objective but you must not lose money.

sections.label: LTA roles and team unity
sections.summary: The speaker mentions LTA's three roles and an unspoken fourth role, and the importance of working as one team.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: As far as LTA is concerned, the three roles and the unspoken fourth role.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: But the importance of working as one team − especially at the stage where SMRT is in, whereby you have to renew the assets of North-South-East-West Lines.

sections.label: Meaningful job benefiting commuters
sections.summary: The speaker says taking on this job is meaningful and fixing it would be a good public service benefiting millions of daily users.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: But I think it is a meaningful job that we decide to take on, whether it is Desmond Kuek or Seah Moon Ming.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: But if we can fix this, turn it around, it will be a good public service that will benefit three million, 3.5 million people who make use of our system every day.

sections.label: Running services within available revenue
sections.summary: The speaker says they try to run as good a show as possible within collected revenue and government subsidy, describing it as a four to five-year journey.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: We do our best and within the revenue that we can collect from the people and with the subsidy we get from the Government − that means from the taxpayers − we try to run as good a show as we can.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: But as I have shared with this House, it is a four-year, five-year journey.
